title: Smooth disabled-opacity and icon-stack loading affordance for small action buttons
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Several products reported visual regressions and confusing behavior when small icon-only and compact compound buttons toggle between active, loading, and disabled states across theme variants (light/dark/high-contrast). Current behavior: abrupt opacity jumps when disabling a control, spinner overlays that hide affordance and remove tap targets, and inconsistent icon color contrast in disabled tokens. Impact: perceived UI jank, tappable area regressions on mobile, accessibility issues for low-vision users, and flaky visual tests that block shipping. Goal: define a consistent, theme-aware visual contract for compact and icon buttons covering three primary states: idle (default), transient-loading (optimistic/ cancellable), and final-disabled (non-interactive). The contract must be token-driven, animate smoothly without layout shift, retain clear hit targets, and satisfy WCAG contrast where applicable. This ticket covers design spec, motion guidelines, tokens required, example code snippets for engineers, and acceptance criteria for QA and regressions.
motivation: Reduce regressions and onboarding friction for engineers consuming button tokens; provide an opinionated transition that preserves tap targets and communicates interruptibility for short network operations. Align with runtime batching/optimistic UX patterns used by infra and SDK teams so visual and functional fallbacks are predictable.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce two discrete token groups: button.state.opacity (idle, transientLoading, disabled) and button.state.tint (icon-color overrides per theme). 2) Replace instant opacity toggles with a short ease-out transition (120ms) for opacity and a subtle scale-down (98%) over the same duration when moving to 'transientLoading'. 3) For transientLoading: overlay a 18px spinner baked into left/right icon slot (not centered over content) with 48x48 hit-area preserved via invisible padding; spinner uses token button.spinner.color that adapts to theme. 4) For finalDisabled: reduce interactive affordance visually to target opacity 0.36 (light) / 0.28 (dark) with no spinner and disable pointer events. 5) Ensure tokens include high-contrast overrides and an opt-in reduced-motion variant (motion: none -> crossfade-only). 6) Provide CSS/React implementation notes for engineers including aria attributes for cancellable loading (aria-busy, aria-disabled toggles, aria-live for status changes).
acceptance_criteria: Visual spec produced in Figma for 3 sizes: compact(32px), small(40px), regular(48px) showing idle/transientLoading/disabled across light/dark/high-contrast
Transitions: opacity + scale executed in <= 120ms with easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); reduced-motion reduces animation to simple opacity change
No layout shift: spinner occupies reserved slot; hit target remains >= 44px in all sizes
WCAG contrast maintained for icon color in disabled state where customer_impact != none
Engineering PR merges with unit/visual tests and storybook examples demonstrating cancelable loading flow
QA checklist green: keyboard focus/activation preserved, ARIA announcements for loading start/end, screen reader reads 'cancellable' state when appropriate

ui_notes: Spinner placement: for icon-only buttons spinner replaces icon with fade and reserved spacing; for compound buttons spinner appears in same slot as leading icon to avoid centering over label
Hit area preservation: use token button.padding.inset for invisible padding to meet minimum tappable target
Interaction pattern: transientLoading should expose an escape (cancel) pattern where relevant; include small 'x' dismiss in adjacent contextual toolbar instead of overloading the icon button
Theme-aware tints: disabled icon color should not rely solely on opacity; use dedicated tint tokens to avoid contrast regression when backgrounds are non-standard
accessibility_considerations: Use aria-busy on parent element during transientLoading
Set aria-disabled=true only for finalDisabled; during transientLoading leave focusable and expose cancel mechanism
Announce loading start/end via aria-live polite region when operation lasts > 250ms
Ensure color tokens meet 3:1 contrast for non-text icons where interactive state implies meaning; opt for 4.5:1 where icons convey critical status
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Teams may misuse transientLoading and treat it as disabled -> mitigation: include clear examples and codemod to replace direct disabled toggles with loading API
Risk: Visual tests flaky due to timing-> mitigation: make animation durations configurable in test environment and freeze to 0ms
Risk: Theme edge-cases on custom backgrounds-> mitigation: provide fallback tokens and an explicit guidance doc for overriding tokens
